semanticText:
# Confirmation Clause

Manages one current, exact proposal and a confirmed service start for each fulfilment group. It separates supplier approval, customer acceptance of changes or immediate cancellation charges, and recorded fulfilment.

## Bindings and initialization

`bindings.snapshot` defaults to `/orderSnapshot` and supplies the accepted quote, terms, group selections and supplier readiness. `bindings.state` defaults to `/reservations` and stores groups keyed by group ID. `bindings.requests` defaults to `/reservationRequests` and records accepted action intents and their resulting status. These are configurable document pointers; changing them changes where the clause reads and writes.

`initialize` runs automatically once on clause initialization. Both `state` and `requests` must already equal `{}`; missing values are not empty-state defaults. Initialization checks `quoteBlueId` and `termsBlueId` against their respective values. There must be 1–20 uniquely identified groups, each containing at least one zero-based `lineIndices` entry. Every quote line belongs to exactly one group, and a group cannot contain different supplied `serviceDate` values.

Snapshot `terms` requires `fulfilmentText`, `agreementDescription` and `confirmationMode`. `confirmationMode` is `supplier` or `automatic`. Optional Boolean `dateRequired` defaults to false during initialization and, when true, requires each initial `proposedStartMicros`. An exact start is required before confirmation regardless of this setting.

In `supplier` mode, groups begin `pending_supplier`. In `automatic` mode, `supplierReadiness.quoteBlueId` and `supplierReadiness.groups` must exactly match the snapshot. The start must be later than `acceptedAtMicros`; qualifying immediate cancellation charges require snapshot `acceptImmediateCharge: true`. Successful automatic initialization records `confirmed` and uses `acceptedAtMicros` as `confirmedAtMicros`.

## Actions and outcomes

Every non-initialization action requires `key`, `groupId` and `expectedProposalBlueId`. Unknown fields, unknown groups and stale proposal identities are rejected. A reused key returns `duplicate` only when action, calling channel and complete input match the recorded intent; otherwise it conflicts. There may be at most 500 recorded requests. Identifiers must be 1–64 characters, exclude `/` and `~`, not start with `$`, and avoid the reserved names checked by `validateIdentifier`.

- `confirm` operates on `pending_supplier`. Before any response deadline and with a future exact start, it records supplier approval and normally confirms. If a positive cancellation charge would already apply, it instead records `pending_customer` and `immediateChargeConsentRequired: true`.
- `alternative` operates on either pending status before any response deadline. It additionally requires `catalog`, `lines` and `proposedStartMicros`. The catalog must have the original supplier and currency, and the start must be future. It prices a replacement quote, appends a numbered proposal to `history`, records supplier approval and changes the status to `pending_customer`. There can be at most 20 proposals, including the initial one. An existing response deadline remains in force.
- `accept` operates on `pending_customer`, requires `supplierApproved: true`, a future proposed start and an unpassed response deadline, and records `confirmed`. Optional Boolean `acceptImmediateCharge` defaults to false for this action and must be true when a positive cancellation charge would already apply.
- `deadline` additionally requires `deadlineMicros`. It sets `responseDeadlineMicros` once for a pending group, strictly after the invocation timestamp. Setting a deadline does not itself schedule expiry. At or after it, new `confirm`, `alternative` and `accept` requests are rejected.
- `fulfil` changes `confirmed` to `fulfilled` and records `fulfilledAtMicros`, only at or after `confirmedStartMicros`.

Supplier and customer are the business roles of these transitions. Actual invocation sources, authenticated workflow channels, parameter mappings and additional conditions come from configured connections; these action bodies do not independently enforce those role names. Only initialization has a built-in connection. A callable action alone establishes neither permission nor an obligation.

A successful new transition saves the group and request record, emits `Reservation Changed`, and returns `acceptedNew`. A request record's `status` is the resulting group status at that time, not a pending external operation. Duplicate outcomes do not repeat the transition or run configured `after` steps. Confirmation and recorded fulfilment do not establish payment or independently verify physical service delivery.

## Proposals, prices and time

A proposal contains `number`, `quote`, `quoteBlueId`, `lineIndices`, `amountMinor` and, when supplied, `proposedStartMicros`. `amountMinor` is the stored sum of the selected quote lines' `lineTotalMinor`, in `quote.currency`; it is a proposed service price, not reserved or paid funds. An initial proposal retains the whole order quote, so only its `lineIndices` identify that group's items. An alternative selects all lines of its replacement quote.

Quote lines preserve `itemLabel`, optional `itemDescription`, `quantity`, `pricingUnit`, `unitAmountMinor`, `billableUnits`, `subtotalMinor`, `guestDiscountPercent`, `discountMinor` and `lineTotalMinor`. `per_unit` uses quantity; `per_selected_hour` also uses an offered integer `durationHours` from 1–168. Alternatives contain 1–20 selections, obey catalog quantity limits and reject duplicate item/date/duration selections. A catalog-required `serviceDate` must be a valid calendar date in 2000–2099; otherwise it is forbidden. It is distinct from the exact service-start instant. An omitted catalog discount becomes zero during pricing; discounts are rounded half-up per line. All monetary fields use the enclosing quote's currency.

Optional `terms.cancellationPolicy` requires integer `freeCancellationHoursBeforeStart` from 0–8760 and `lateCancellationChargePercent` from 0–100. Confirmation uses zero for both when the policy is omitted, but does not persist `freeCancellationUntilMicros` without a policy. With a policy, that field records the cutoff before the confirmed start. Immediate-charge consent is required strictly after the cutoff, only when the half-up rounded cancellation charge is positive; equality does not trigger it. This is consent to cancellation exposure, not a payment request.

The `Micros` instant fields use Unix microseconds. Missing lifecycle fields are generally unknown, not false, zero or evidence of completion. In particular, automatic confirmation need not write `supplierApproved`, and missing `freeCancellationUntilMicros` may reflect an omitted cancellation policy.
